text:
mike: Heads-up — planning a terraform apply tied to today's release v1.9. Touches: route53 zone updates + cross-account VPC peering + a small IAM role change. Quiet/change window 02:00-03:00 UTC tonight. Can ops + network weigh in?
ryan: :+1: I can own the oncall rotation for that window. Recommend canary first in us-east-1 single-AZ.
jen: We'll pin provider and module refs in tfvars (provider = 3.2.0). Also add explicit module version lock to avoid surprises.
sara: Can we add a deploybot override tag so we can abort fast from the console? Also suggest freezing the merge queue 30m before window.
deploybot: deploybot: running preflight checks now...
deploybot: deploybot: preflight: running `terraform init && terraform plan` (workspace: release-v1.9)
deploybot: deploybot: plan result: 1 error in iam_roles, 2 proposed changes in aws_route53_record, 1 vpc_peering creation.
jen: paste plan snippet:
```
# module.vpc_peering.aws_vpc_peering_connection.peer will be created
+ resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection" "peer" {
  + id = (known after apply)
}
# module.dns.aws_route53_record.www will be updated
~ ttl = 300 -> 60
```
mike: infra-bot, any drift alerts we should know about?
infra-bot: infra-bot: detected drift: route53 zone Z1234 TTLs were changed outside of terraform (timestamps: 2024-01-10). Recommend adding a quick reconciliation step and notifying DNS owners.
sara: Noted. I'll open a follow-up ticket but we should reconcile in the canary only, not global.
ryan: Canary plan (my steps):
1) run `terraform apply -target=module.vpc_canary -var='region=us-east-1' -auto-approve`
2) wait 10 minutes, smoke test connectivity
3) run `terraform apply -target=module.dns_canary -var='region=us-east-1'` if green
Please post outputs verbatim in this channel.
jen: Rollback playbook (short):
- If IAM apply fails or unexpected denies: revoke policy changes via console + run `git revert <commit>` then `terraform apply -target=module.iam -auto-approve`
- If DNS change causes outage: revert route53 record to previous value via console and run `terraform apply` for reconciliation.
- Escape hatch: cut traffic to backup region using the LB health switch documented in the runbook.
jen: commands for quick revert:
```
git revert <sha>
git push origin HEAD:release-v1.9
terraform apply -parallelism=1 -auto-approve
```
oncall-ops: I'll be live in the channel 01:50-03:30 UTC. If deploybot shows >50% resource failures we abort and start rollback. Also, if error rate >5% in prod we trigger emergency rollback.
mike: Added release notes section for infra changes and contact list. Tagging @sre and @security. Merge queue will be locked at 01:30 UTC.
sara: I'll lock merges at 01:30 and unlock after 04:00 if all good.
jen: Added provider pin in tfvars + updated module refs. Pushed commit and opened PR with runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/infra-apply-evac
deploybot: deploybot: preflight complete — plan shows: 1 IAM change, 2 Route53 changes, 1 VPC peering. No provider upgrade. No blocking drift after reconcile step. Ready for canary.
mike: Proceeding with canary at 02:10 UTC. Canary target: us-east-1. If green for 10m, we roll to remaining regions with staged apply (10m watch per region).
ryan: Canary apply started at 02:10 UTC. Output (partial):
```
Apply complete! Resources: 2 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed.
Outputs:
canary_vpc_peering_id = "pcx-0a1b2c3d"
```
sara: Seeing DNS propagation lag in eu-west-1 for the test record — TTL drop to 60 is causing some caching. Monitoring.
jen: If we need to abort full rollout: run `git revert <sha>` then `terraform apply -target=module.dns -auto-approve` and notify SRE to cut traffic.
ryan: Canary looks stable for 12m, proceeding to staged rollout for the next region at 02:25 UTC.
mike: Reminder: metrics to watch — 5xx rate, route53 errors, cross-account VPC metrics. If any spike, warn and abort.
oncall-ops: Confirmed. If deploybot posts more than 3 fails within 5m we trigger rollback.
mike: Great work — will post final status when all regions are done. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
